subject: Octave Health — production error surge & SLA impact
messages:
From: Aanya Rao <aanya@octave.health>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s — inference requests failing intermittently

Hi Monica,

We started seeing a burst of 5xx and 429 errors on the Redwood endpoint for production around 08:45 PT this morning. Traffic pattern unchanged on our side; errors correlate with slightly elevated latencies followed by sudden 5xx spikes. Our app experienced a retry amplification that caused request rates to climb further for ~12 minutes.

Attached is an abbreviated log with a few request IDs and timestamps (error-snippet.log). Key symptoms:
- ~20% 5xx rate during the 08:45–08:58 window
- Multiple 429s coincident with queueing events
- Timeouts at client ~10s; server returned 500/503 for many requests

This is impacting a production feature (clinical predictions). We need immediate triage and ETA to restore normal levels. Can your team confirm whether this looks like a capacity/autoscaler issue on your side?

Thanks,
Aanya Rao
SRE, Octave Health

Attachments: error-snippet.log (text/plain)
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Aanya Rao <aanya@octave.health>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s — inference requests failing intermittently

Thanks Aanya — and sorry for the disruption. We're triaging this now and I've looped in Platform and Eng (Markus + Vivek).

Initial ask: could you paste one full request ID and timestamp (from the log) so we can correlate in our tracing? We're pulling host-level metrics for the dedicated pool serving your account. Early guess from the surface symptoms: short-lived autoscaler lag + queueing leading to timeouts and retry amplification.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Platform: examine autoscaler events and GPU pool allocation (Markus)
- Thundering herd check: temporarily disable aggressive client retries if possible (Octave SRE)
- If we see autoscaling behind, we'll push short-term capacity (reserved burst) and route traffic to a sibling pool to buy time

I'll keep you updated every 20–30 minutes. Can we schedule a 30-min bridge at 12:00 PT to go over the postmortem and mitigation once we have a root-cause?

—
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Available: +1 415-555-0142

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 9:23 AM monica_patel@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Aanya — and sorry for the disruption. We're triaging this now and I've looped in Platform and Eng (Markus + Vivek).

Quick update from Platform triage: we see the Dedicated GPU pool for Octave Health hit node saturation as the request concurrency increased. The autoscaler did trigger, but there is a ~45–60s lag before new nodes are fully provisioned and warmed due to kernel JIT and model weight loading. During that window we observed downstream queueing which surfaced as 429s and then 5xx as timeouts cascaded.

Evidence attached: brief export of autoscaler events and timestamps (autoscaler-events.csv). Graphs (Grafana) show an immediate spike in pod queue length and a delayed node add.

Short-term remediation (what we can do in next 15–30 mins):
- Promote reserved burst capacity for Octave to reduce queueing immediately (we can route to burst pool and pre-warm instances)
- Apply a soft throttle on client-side retry headers (Retry-After) while we stabilize
- If acceptable, route a small percentage of traffic to a lightly-quantized model variant to reduce load during warm-up

I will be on the bridge if you want to authorize the capacity bump.

—
Markus Klein
Head of Platform, Redwood Inference
Attachments: autoscaler-events.csv
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s — inference requests failing intermittently

Thanks for the fast triage. High level for execs/CS: this looks like an autoscaler cold-warm gap compounded by an amplification loop from client retries. We're treating this as a Sev-2 (customer-impacting, needs mitigation and postmortem).

Requested immediate approvals:
- Temporary reserved burst (up to +30% of their committed pool) — we can absorb cost for the next 24h if needed
- Customer-facing note: short update within 1 hour and a commitment to an RCA within 48h

Monica — please confirm you have approval to authorize the burst. I'll join the 12:00 PT bridge for the postmortem.

Vivek
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Aanya Rao <aanya@octave.health>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:58:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in 5xx/429s — inference requests failing intermittently

Aanya — quick update and next steps. TL;DR: we've applied a temporary burst capacity and reduced routing to the saturated pool; error rates are back to baseline (~1–2%). We're keeping the burst for the next 24 hours while we complete a short RCA.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:40 PT: detected pod queueing and autoscaler add delay (Markus)
- 09:46 PT: authorized +30% burst capacity; pre-warmed instances and rerouted 40% of traffic to burst pool
- 09:52 PT: client retry headers honored; we asked Octave to temporarily add a conservative Retry-After of 3s (if you can)
- 09:58 PT: observed 5xx/429 rates drop sharply and latency normalize

Attachments: incident-runbook.pdf (short incident notes), autoscaler-events.csv, error-snippet.log (from Aanya)

Next steps:
- 12:00 PT: bridge for postmortem and runbook review (we'll share screens and Grafana panels)
- 48h: RCA with timeline, root cause, and follow-up mitigations (autoscaler tuning + warm pool strategy + client retry guidance)

We will proactively cover the incremental cost from the burst for the next 24h. Apologies again for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority and will share the RCA as soon as available.

Best,
Monica Patel
